title: How to Spend a Sunday in Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **Normal shops, supermarkets and chemists are usually shut on a Berlin Sunday** under the Berlin Shop Opening Act. Exceptions include station supermarkets, emergency pharmacies, some limited product ranges, hospitality, and museums.

**Start at a flea market.** Mauerpark in Prenzlauer Berg (10am to 6pm), Boxhagener Platz in Friedrichshain (10am to 6pm), Arkonaplatz (year-round) and the Nowkoelln Flowmarkt in Neukölln on selected published dates. Bring cash.
**Mauerpark is the Sunday centrepiece.** From roughly May to October, free open-air Bearpit Karaoke fills the stone amphitheatre from about 3pm, weather permitting.
**Sunday is a great museum day; Monday is the one to avoid.** Most Museum Island venues run Sunday hours. The Pergamonmuseum is fully closed and a large part is scheduled to reopen on 4 June 2027.
**When the sun is out, go outside.** Tempelhofer Feld, the Landwehrkanal, Tiergarten and the lakes such as Strandbad Weißensee are the local Sunday. Buy your picnic first, because the shops are shut.
**Transport runs a normal Sunday timetable.** The U-Bahn only runs all night on Friday and Saturday, so check your last train on a Sunday night. Ferries count on a normal ticket.
